articles.content: When AI builds itself \ Anthropic Skip to main content Skip to footer Research Economic Futures Commitments Learn News Try Claude When AI builds itself Our progress toward recursive self-improvement, and its implications. For most of AI’s history, humans drove every step in its development cycle. But at Anthropic, we are delegating a growing share of AI development to AI systems themselves, which is speeding up our work. Taken far enough, and given enough compute, that trend points to an AI system capable of fully autonomously designing and developing its own successor. This is called recursive self-improvement . We are not there yet, and recursive self-improvement is not inevitable. But it could come sooner than most institutions are prepared for. Using public benchmarks and previously un

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Kilo bet the other way from day one. Transparent pricing, BYOK, 500+ models, no surcharge. You should never have to care which lab controls the weights or where the compute lives. Model choice is a right, not a premium feature you unlock at checkout.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Which is the actual punchline. The pitch for years was "pick one vendor, buy the subscription, get on with it." Convenient. Right up until that vendor reprices overnight, deprecates the model you depend on, or decides your tier no longer includes what it used to.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Then there's the SpaceX–Cursor deal. Everyone read it as a productivity story. It isn't. A rocket company wiring a million-H100-equivalent supercomputer to a coding tool, with a $60B option to buy, is a compute-alignment deal. Cursor sits at the demand layer, deciding where your requests get routed. Standardize on it and you're not picking an assistant, you're locking your throughput to one vendor's roadmap.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Anthropic did a softer version of the same move, steering people off flat subscriptions toward pay-per-token API access. Different press release, identical math. Compute is expensive, subsidies don't scale, and the bill always comes due.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: GitHub's own CPO said the quiet part out loud: a quick chat question and a multi-hour autonomous session used to cost you the same, and they ate the difference. That's done. Each plan now includes credits equal to its price. $10 for Pro. When they're gone, there's no free fallback.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: The era of free compute is over. GitHub Copilot moving to usage-based billing on June 1 isn't a one-off pricing tweak. It's the whole industry quietly admitting the all-you-can-eat model was never sustainable. We've been saying this for a while. 🧵
